title: The category of poset-indexed diagrams and its filtered unions
statement: For a category C and universe w, form the category of diagrams U:I→C with I a partial order in Type w. A morphism (I,U)→(J,V) is an order embedding e:I↪oJ with equality U=e⋙V; composition composes embeddings and these equalities. This category has colimits indexed by any small filtered category A in Type w, and its index functor to PartOrdEmb preserves these colimits. The index colimit embeddings are jointly surjective on elements.

source.place: Tag 00YP, proof of lemma-refine-all-at-once; strict refinements preceding Tag 00YO

proof.text: Take the filtered colimit of the index posets in Mathlib PartOrdEmb. Its underlying type is the filtered colimit of their underlying types. The object assignments agree on transition embeddings, so their cocone descends to an object assignment on the union.

source.place: Tag 00YP, proof of lemma-refine-all-at-once; strict refinements preceding Tag 00YO

proof.text: For i≤j in the union, choose a stage representing both elements and their order relation. Define the transition by the stage diagram, transported through the object equalities. Two such representatives agree after mapping to a common stage: injectivity of its embedding identifies the endpoints, and equality of restricted diagrams identifies the arrows. A common stage containing three indices proves composition; the diagonal proves identity.

source.place: Tag 00YP, proof of lemma-refine-all-at-once; strict refinements preceding Tag 00YO

proof.text: Stage diagrams agree with the restricted union functor. For a competing cocone, descend its index embeddings by the PartOrdEmb colimit property. Joint surjectivity and the same order-pair representation show equality of the restricted functors. This gives the unique morphism from the union and proves the colimit property and preservation by the index functor.
